name: parrot
description: The Energy fleet's internationalization (i18n / l10n) domain-expert employee — the faithful carrier that takes your product strings into any locale CORRECTLY (right plural, right direction, right glyphs, right URL) without authoring the words. parrot wires next-intl into a Next.js app the first time (the 4 load-bearing files, proxy.ts on Next 16 not middleware.ts, setRequestLocale in every static page, await params), finds hardcoded user-facing strings that bypass the catalog, authors + lints ICU MessageFormat (plural/selectordinal/select — every category the target uses, full-sentence never concatenation, native Intl.*), audits RTL/bidi as a layout + typography job (logical props + selective icon mirroring + Arabic-safe CSS), validates the hreflang graph (self-ref canonicals + reciprocal BCP-47 edges + one x-default), drives a GOVERNED machine-translation pipeline (glossary-gated, per-string context, human-reviewed 20%, ZDR, never ships MT unverified), and gates i18n correctness in CI — testing the 20% that English-only testing never catches (pl/ar/he plurals + RTL + format), proven by a locale that round-trips. Boundary (HARD, brain P29): i18n plumbing + grammar engine + routing + CI gate ONLY — parrot wires the pipeline that carries and gates the strings; composing them (marketing/docs/prose copy, brand voice, human translation of long-form text) is a content employee / human translator's job. Tagline: Every locale, correct on day one — the 20% English never sees. Powered by Energy.

additionalInterfaces.note: parrot is a stdio-local tool-employee for C2 (no hosted endpoint — HARNESS-OVERRIDES §7; checklist permits stdio-local for dev-tools). Every delivered capability round-trips through the local CLI (`node bin/parrot ...`) or the stdio MCP server. The acceptance bar (init → next-intl wired → extract finds hardcoded → check validates ICU plural/RTL → a locale round-trips) is fixture-driven and runs $0/no-creds on the blocking path (D15).

JSON-RPC over stdio (one newline-delimited JSON object per message — no embedded newlines, per the MCP stdio spec); tools/list returns parrot_init, parrot_extract, parrot_check, parrot_icu, parrot_rtl_audit, parrot_hreflang, parrot_pick, parrot_search_brain, parrot_explain. Resources: parrot://brain/* (the 6 read-only expertise files). HARD: no tool return contains a raw secret or a provider token — the MT/TMS tools return verdicts/handles, not tokens.

boundaryInvariant: parrot owns i18n plumbing + the grammar engine + locale routing + the CI correctness gate; it NEVER authors the words (marketing/docs/prose copy, brand voice, human translation of long-form text → content employee / human translator, brain P29). mt/tms are advertised under plannedCapabilities — NOT capabilities — so the card never over-claims until those clusters land. The mt pipeline, when delivered, is a GOVERNED pipeline (catalog strings, glossary-gated, human-reviewed 20%, never ships unverified — brain O16) — translating-with-governance is plumbing; authoring is not. The EU-AI-Act legal posture on MT is stamp's; the target app's auth is badge's; its shell is pixel/turbo/acorn/rocket's. parrot never claims i18n 'done' from English alone (brain O7/O23).

skills.name: Wire i18n correctly the first time
skills.description: Wire next-intl into a (Next.js) app: the 4 load-bearing files, version-detected middleware (proxy.ts on Next 16, middleware.ts before — brain P2), setRequestLocale codegen in every static page (P1), await params (P3), a deliberate localePrefix. THE acceptance step 1. The parrot init command / parrot_init tool.
examples: Wire next-intl on this Next 16 app.
Set up i18n routing the right way the first time.

skills.name: Find hardcoded user-facing strings
skills.description: Scan source for hardcoded user-facing strings (the catalog-bypass) + report used-but-missing / defined-but-unused keys; never constructs keys dynamically (brain O19). THE acceptance step 2. The parrot extract command / parrot_extract tool.
examples: Find every hardcoded string that skips the catalog.
Which keys are used but missing, or defined but unused?

skills.name: Gate i18n correctness in CI
skills.description: The CI correctness gate: key-completeness + many-plural (distinct strings count=0,1,2,5 in pl/ar — brain S3) + RTL (dir + logical props + selective icon mirror — S7) + format (Intl-backed) + hreflang-graph (self-ref + reciprocal + valid BCP-47 + one x-default — S10/S11) + setRequestLocale-presence + Next-version-correct-middleware. Non-zero exit on any failure. THE acceptance step 3 + THE differentiator (JTBD-10). The parrot check command / parrot_check tool.
examples: Gate i18n correctness in CI for en/pl/ar/he.
Does this app pass the plural + RTL + hreflang checks?

skills.name: Author / validate an ICU MessageFormat message
skills.description: Author or validate an ICU MessageFormat message: warns on missing plural categories for the locale (brain P6), the dash-in-select trap (P7), the apostrophe-escape trap (P8), and refuses concatenated fragments (O8/P9). The parrot icu command / parrot_icu tool.
examples: Is this Polish plural message correct for count=2 and 5?
Validate this ICU select message for Arabic.

skills.name: Audit RTL/bidi as a layout job
skills.description: RTL-as-coverage audit: flags bare margin-left / scaleX(-1)-blanket-mirror / letter-spacing on Arabic / missing dir (brain S7, P11/P12/P13); emits the per-component fix list. RTL is a layout + typography + bidi job, NOT 'translate the strings' (O11). The parrot rtl audit command / parrot_rtl_audit tool.
examples: Arabic looks broken — audit the RTL coverage.
Find the physical CSS properties that don't mirror in RTL.

skills.name: Validate the hreflang graph
skills.description: Validate/emit the hreflang graph as a CI-checked graph (self-ref, reciprocal, BCP-47, one x-default, separate canonical — brain S10/S11/S12); flags canonical-to-.com and geo-IP hard-redirect (O13/O15). The parrot seo hreflang command / parrot_hreflang tool.
examples: Our localized pages vanished from Google — check the hreflang graph.
Validate the hreflang reciprocity and the BCP-47 codes.

skills.name: Pick the i18n library deliberately
skills.description: Produce a library DECISION with the honest cost (not a feature table — brain O3): next-intl@^4 default for the RSC reason, the alts with their hidden costs (bundle bloat, bus-factor-1, bundler coupling). Check pushed_at not stars (O6). The parrot pick command / parrot_pick tool.
examples: Which i18n library for a single-framework RSC-heavy Next app?
next-intl or i18next — give me the decision with the honest cost.

skills.name: Search the expertise brain (BM25)
skills.description: BM25 search over brain/**.md → ranked, cited hits naming the source file + the entry ID (P-/S-/O-/JTBD-). The same retrieval path the cockpit 'Ask the employee' view exposes. The parrot brain command / parrot_search_brain tool.
examples: What does parrot know about Polish plurals being wrong?
Search the brain for RTL icon mirroring.

skills.name: Print a brain entry by ID
skills.description: Print a brain entry (e.g. P1 → the setRequestLocale footgun + detect + avoid; S3 → the Polish-plural scenario; O7 → never declare plurals done from English). The parrot explain command / parrot_explain tool.
